_doc: skin_tokens.example.json — brand tokens for a film skin (fictional Acme defaults = the colours film.example.html ships with today).
A skin is a flat set of typed slots plus the v5 sections (type, motion, captions, seams, when_to_use) — ten complete ones live in
skins/ (skins/README.md); tools/brand_kit.py extracts or composes a new one and draws its style sheet; `brand_kit.py check` gates it.
HOW A SCENE APPLIES THE TOKENS (one flag): film.json "skin": "skins/<name>.json" -> build_film.py step 0 runs
python tools/skin_apply.py skins/<name>.json   ->  scenes/skin_data.js  (+ design.md tokens rewritten from the skin)
scenes/skin_data.js is a plain local script: it sets window.SKIN = <this document> and, synchronously at load, every style/layout
token as a CSS custom property on document.documentElement — colour and font slots -> `--<id>: <value>`, number slots ->
`--<id>: <value><unit>`, enum slots -> `--<id>` plus a data-skin-<id> attribute on <html>; data-skin="<name>" names the look.
The scene includes it ONCE, right after its <style> block and before any script that measures layout:
<script src="skin_data.js"></script>
Its CSS already reads var(--paper), var(--ink), var(--accent), var(--black) … with these defaults on :root, so a film without a
skin renders exactly as before, and a skinned film is re-coloured before the first __seek. Content slots (title, subtitle,
caption, logo) are NOT pushed into the DOM automatically: SKIN.bind(document) fills only EMPTY bound elements (`binds`), so
authored FILM.* copy always wins; shots.js may read SKIN.motion.* and SKIN.captions.style as its defaults (guidance, never the clock).
There is no ?skin= query or fetch() path: a file: scene cannot fetch, and a generated local script is what lint_scene.py and the
determinism canary can see. To preview another look, run skin_apply.py again with another skin (studio hot-reloads the scene).
HEAD FADE: the scene's #black plate is `background: var(--black)`; light skins set black = paper (brand_kit does this for every
light ground), so a light film opens from its own paper, never a dark flash. build_film.py compares frame 0 with the plate;
tools/export.py dips the booth loop to the same token. Precedence: skin file > the :root values authored in the scene.
What can NEVER be a token: the narration text (it is the clock), fps, 1920x1080, the total length, the codec, and the mandatory
FDE Demo Builder credit (credit.py picks its own colour from the end screen). `portrays` tags mark identity slots: subject_* must
stay fictional in examples, host_identity (the depicted product's own UI) is never repainted.
Prove a re-skin differentially: render one still with the skin and one with a probe skin (paper/ink inverted); > 5 % of 160x90
grey pixels must differ, else the binding never reached the DOM (tools/skin_apply.py --selftest checks the loader in a DOM stub).
name: acme-night

gold.description: first line of the closing card

title-font.description: title + closing card face (local @font-face or a system family)

title-size.description: title h1 size on the 1280x720 stage

subtitle.default: From an analyst’s notebook to a question anyone can ask

caption.description: the honesty line; keep it unless the film shows a real customer's own data with their approval

logo.description: local file inside the project (assets/…); null hides the slot

density.description: booth = larger type, fewer words on screen

_doc: Batch re-skin: rows.json → one film per row. Each row = token overrides merged over this skin + an output name.
The narration clock, VO and footage lane are shared; only the picture is re-rendered per row (skins change pixels), the
audio master is reused unless a row changes bed_db. Output template keys: {name}, {index} and any string/number/boolean
row key; a missing placeholder or two rows mapping to one output is an error. Rows that try to set a forbidden token
(narration, fps, size, total, codec, credit) are refused. Every output still passes qa_film.py and the CREDIT gate.
PLANNED (not in build_film.py yet): build_film.py --batch rows.json --output "out/{name}.mp4" writing out/batch_manifest.json.
Today: one skin per build — write a skin per row (tools/brand_kit.py compose), point film.json "skin" at it and build again.
